verdicts.note: The v6 facts hold (6.0.0-alpha.0, 2026-08-11: error handler overrides disabled by default; FSTDEP022 to 025 removed), but both enforcement claims go too far.
verdicts.correction: allowErrorHandlerOverride: false only rejects a second setErrorHandler in the same scope. Fastify resets the flag in every child context (lib/plugin-override.js: instance[kErrorHandlerAlreadySet] = false), so a module plugin under /v1/<module> can still install its own handler without any error. The single-root-handler rule needs a behavioural check instead: a scenario that makes each module throw and asserts the root error shape. --throw-deprecation turns every DeprecationWarning in the process into an exception, not only Fastify's FSTDEP codes. A deprecation inside Better Auth, pg or Drizzle would therefore turn CI red and could hold up a security update that line 720 lets skip the waiting period. Fail only on FSTDEP codes, or run the flag in a separate job that does not block security updates.

recommendation_issues.problem: If the phone or panel parses responses at runtime with the shared Zod schemas, a strict z.enum rejects any value added later. That contradicts the plan's tolerant-client rule (line 580) and additive-only /v1 (line 723): phones already in students' hands would fail on a new label. The plan text must say that response types are imported type-only, or that response enums are parsed leniently with a fallback for unknown values. packages/contracts must also stay free of Fastify and Node imports so that the phone bundle never pulls in server code.

Switching now means pinning @fastify/type-provider-zod 1.0.0 (2026-04-19). That release is older than the community 7.0.0 (2026-06-24) and lacks fixes that reached the official main branch only on 2026-09-10 and are still unreleased. It fails the 'current' lens today. Switch at the official package's next release instead.

--throw-deprecation applies to the whole process, so it would fail CI on third-party deprecations and could stall security updates. allowErrorHandlerOverride does not catch a handler set inside a module plugin, so the promised red test never fires for the case the plan cares about.

Moving Better Auth's basePath under /v1 adds no detection power and mixes third-party endpoints into the additive-only /v1 promise. Better Auth itself calls the openAPI plugin early-stage, so the plan should not present it as the guard.

Keying the submit limit by device works only if the key is the verified device. By default the limiter runs in onRequest, before the body and signature are checked, so a client can rotate a self-supplied device id to get around it. Run the per-device limit after signature verification (hook preHandler), and keep a generous per-IP ceiling, sized for NAT, on every route for flood control. Better Auth's own limiter reads x-forwarded-for by default, so the proxy must go into Better Auth's trustedProxies as well as Fastify's trustProxy.
With oasdiff's default levels, 'stop on ERR' blocks response enum additions, which the plan treats as additive. The recommendation must include the severity override or x-extensible-enum.

Line 714 puts the API, worker and xprem in the same Compose file. Run with no service names, 'docker compose up -d --wait' starts them too, and the API container would clash with the server that pnpm dev starts. Name the services (PostgreSQL, Mailpit) or put the app services behind a Compose profile.

misses.finding: The plan puts a proxy in front of the server only at scale-out, and the Docker Compose stack (line 714) has no TLS terminator. Phones cannot use a plain-HTTP API: Android 9 and later disable cleartext by default, and iOS App Transport Security requires TLS. Fastify's own guide calls exposing Node directly to the Internet an anti-pattern that prevents horizontal scaling. The proxy also decides which client IP to trust. Better Auth reads x-forwarded-for by default, and its docs warn that clients can spoof that header when the origin is directly reachable. Until a proxy overwrites the header and trustedProxies is set, the IP-based limits on the code endpoints (line 586) can be bypassed. The plan's later load balancer is this same component, so adding it on day one costs nothing at scale-out.

evidence.quote: The Fastify team strongly considers this to be an anti-pattern and extremely bad practice: (1) It adds unnecessary complexity to the application by diluting its focus. (2) It prevents horizontal scalability.

ATS blocks connections that don't meet minimum security requirements.
Keep your origin reachable only through these proxies, and make each proxy overwrite or sanitize the forwarded IP headers.

misses.finding: By default oasdiff treats adding a value to a response enum as a definite break (ERR). The plan expects response values to grow, for example new record labels such as Doğrulanmış in Aşama 2 or new final statuses, and it relies on tolerant clients. A plain breaking check that fails on ERR would therefore block these additive changes, or tempt the developer to loosen the whole gate. oasdiff offers two built-in ways out: a severity-levels file that downgrades that one check, or x-extensible-enum on the field. The researcher left this as an open question only.

verdict_reason: PASS. The only high-severity finding, S02-01 (openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch frozen), is confirmed by the maintainers' own posts and by the npm registry. Four findings are corrected, none of them high. S02-02: the official Zod type provider's only release is behind the community 7.0.0 today, and it is not on the Ecosystem Core list. S02-04: allowErrorHandlerOverride does not reach child plugins, and --throw-deprecation applies to the whole process. S02-05: the Better Auth risk is overstated, and its openAPI plugin is early-stage. S02-12: oasdiff flags response enum additions as ERR by default. The other nine findings are confirmed, three of them with conditions listed under recommendation_issues. One checked_ok item is disputed on that same oasdiff default. Three misses are added, none high: no TLS-terminating proxy until scale-out (medium), the oasdiff enum default against additive-only /v1 (medium), and load shedding that is off by default with no Retry-After handling (low). Process note: besides npm view, Bash was used twice, once with wc -l to count plan lines and once with curl to grep the public Fastify Ecosystem.md. Both were read-only and wrote no files. The Ecosystem result was re-read through WebFetch.
